title: Code Generation Patterns
concept: How the compiler translates high-level XIOM patterns into efficient machine code — match compilation, closure lifting, enum layout, and more.
why: Understanding how patterns compile explains performance. A match statement can be a jump table or a chain of comparisons — knowing which helps you write faster code.
tips: Dense match on small integers compiles to a jump table — O(1) and faster than if-else chains
Iterator chains compile to single fused loops — zero intermediate collections allocated
Generic functions are monomorphized — zero runtime overhead, but larger binary size
Enum niche optimization packs discriminants into unused bit patterns — smaller, faster
common_mistakes: Writing match on strings expecting jump-table speed — strings compile to if-else chains
Assuming iterators allocate — they compile to fused loops, no allocations
Not using generics because you think they're slow — monomorphization makes them as fast as hand-written code
